findings.location: Published page body: the BMW crossing-convention paragraph and adjacent g_i TikZ sketch.
findings.evidence: The page identifies the top vertices as inputs, says the left input passes over the right, and draws the top-left-to-bottom-right branch uninterrupted. Goodman–Hauschild's [*Affine Birman–Wenzl–Murakami Algebras and Tangles in the Solid Torus*](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0411155), Definition 2.3 (PDF p. 4), also places inputs at the top, while its G_i diagram (PDF p. 6) has the top-right-to-bottom-left branch uninterrupted; Definition 3.1 (PDF p. 15) gives the corresponding BMW skein relation. The assigned batch uses a right-over positive Artin crossing and sets z_B=z_D, so reading this page's left-over sketch as the same generator reverses the skein sign. The page is published and outside batch 83. Its convention sketch needs correction or a consistent alternate parameter map. The assigned A page requires this page; this is a page-level edge, so consumer_id is null.

coverage_note: All 17 assigned items and both assigned pages were read, along with their direct item suppliers, the three A-page prerequisite pages, and the transitive suppliers used for the scalar coefficient-domain and BMW basis arguments. I did not recursively audit every dependency beneath the published Alexander, Markov, and Reidemeister theorem suppliers; the report records the exact statements and local proofs used by batch 83.
